Class LimitKeyConfig

java.lang.Object
grafioschtrader.config.LimitKeyConfig
public abstract class LimitKeyConfig extends Object
Declares Grafioschtrader's lifetime (MAX) limit keys and its pseudo entity names, and registers them with the limit key registry. It replaces the former TenantConfig.initialzie() and the defaultLimitMap constructors, and is the single place where the application says which caps exist.

The registrations live in the application layer so that grafiosch-base and grafiosch-server-base name no grafioschtrader-* class. The daily DAY_CUD and DAY_READ keys are deliberately absent: they are derived from the JPA metamodel plus the pseudo names registered here, which keeps an administrator's reach as wide as it is today, including entities that have no configured default at all.

The defaultValue of a registration is the fresh-install value only. In an installation that ever changed a limit, the value in use is the one the migration copied out of the former globalparameters row. EntityLimitSeedGuardTest checks that the literals in the migration and the defaults here agree.

  • Field Details

    • ENTITY_NAME_SIMULATION_TENANT

      public static final String ENTITY_NAME_SIMULATION_TENANT
      Pseudo entity name for the number of simulation environments. The limit counts tenant rows by id_parent_tenant, which is not expressible as a plain Tenant cap, so it must never be enforced on an ordinary tenant create.
      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • ENTITY_NAME_GTNET_SECURITY_IMPORT

      public static final String ENTITY_NAME_GTNET_SECURITY_IMPORT
      Pseudo entity name for securities created by the GTNet import. Kept separate from the ordinary Security cap so that network synchronisation does not consume a user's manual budget. It carries both a daily CUD limit and a lifetime cap.

    • ENTITY_NAME_TRADING_DAYS_MINUS_YEAR

      public static final String ENTITY_NAME_TRADING_DAYS_MINUS_YEAR
      Pseudo entity name for the daily budget of the trading calendar. Its unit is one stock exchange year touched, not one trading_days_minus row: a calendar is always edited or copied a year at a time, and counting rows would make a single sparse year and a whole copied decade cost almost the same. TradingDaysMinus has no daily key of its own either way — it is not a BaseID entity, so it never appears in the derived daily key space.
      See Also:
